easy.def: The tools and clothes you need for something.
examples: I packed my camping gear.
Put on your gear.
She has all her swim gear.

more.def: The equipment and clothes you need for an activity.
examples: We packed our camping gear in the car.
The hockey players put on their gear.
He carried his fishing gear to the lake.

easy.def: A wheel with bumps that turns another wheel.
examples: The gears turn the wheel.
The clock has small gears.
A bike has gears.

more.def: A wheel with teeth around the edge that fits into other wheels to make machines work.
examples: The gears inside the clock turn together.
A bike has gears that make it easier to go uphill.
The small gear turns the big one.

easy.def: Not exact; true for most things.
examples: The general rule is no running.
I have a general idea.
He gave a general answer.

more.def: Including or true for most people or things, and not exact.
examples: She gave us a general idea of how the game works.
The general rule is to put away your toys.
There was a general feeling of excitement.

easy.def: A very high leader in the army.
examples: The general led his soldiers.
The general gave an order.
A general sat at the table.

more.def: A very high officer in the army.
examples: The general planned the march across the mountains.
Soldiers saluted the general.
The general met with leaders from other countries.
I generally eat at six.
Dogs are generally friendly.
It is generally warm in May.

more.def: In most cases, or most of the time.
examples: I generally eat dinner at six.
The weather here is generally mild in spring.
It is generally warm here in May.
The sun generates heat.
Windmills generate power.
The machine generated sparks.

more.def: To make or produce something, especially power or heat.
examples: Windmills generate power from the wind.
The big engine generates a lot of heat.
A good story can generate laughter in a room.

easy.def: All the people who are about the same age.
examples: My grandparents are an older generation.
The younger generation.
Three generations live in this house.

more.def: All the people born and living around the same time, or the time between a parent and child.
examples: Three generations of our family live in this house.
My grandfather's generation grew up without computers.
Each new generation learns from the last.
It was generous of you to share your snack.
The generous girl gave me half her snack.
My aunt is generous with hugs.

more.def: Willing to give time, money, or help to others freely.
examples: Our generous neighbor gave vegetables from her garden to everyone on the street.
He was generous with his time and helped every student.
A generous gift helped the town build a new playground.

easy.def: Having to do with the traits passed from parents to children.
examples: Eye color is genetic.
The trait is genetic.
A genetic code.

more.def: Having to do with genes, the parts of cells that pass traits from parents to children.
examples: Eye color is a genetic trait.
The scientist studied genetic differences.
Curly hair can be genetic.

easy.def: A person who is very, very smart.
examples: He is a genius.
The genius solved the puzzle.
A genius made it.

more.def: A person who has an unusually high ability to think or create.
examples: The young girl was a math genius.
The scientist was a genius.
The musician was a genius who wrote songs at age five.
Be gentle with the baby.
The gentle horse let me pet it.
Use a gentle voice in the library.

more.def: Kind, calm, and careful; not rough or strong.
examples: A gentle rain fell on the garden all morning.
The nurse was gentle when she cleaned the cut.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.

easy.def: A man who is polite and kind.
examples: The gentleman held the door for us.
Grandpa is a true gentleman.
Two gentlemen sat on a bench.

more.def: A man who is polite and well-behaved, or any man when you are speaking politely.
examples: The old gentleman tipped his hat to everyone he met.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats because the show is starting.
A gentleman always lets others go first through the door.
Pet the cat gently.
She patted the baby gently.
He held the bird gently.

more.def: In a soft and careful way that does not hurt.
examples: Pet the puppy gently.
The nurse gently wrapped the bandage.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.
The gold is genuine.
He has a genuine smile.
The coin is genuine.
The coin is made of genuine gold.
She gave me a genuine smile.
The painting turned out to be genuine.
She is genuinely kind.
I am genuinely sorry.
He was genuinely happy.

more.def: In a way that is honest and real, not pretend.
examples: She was genuinely happy to see her grandmother.
I am genuinely sorry that I broke your toy.
He genuinely loves to read about space.

easy.def: A hand movement that means something.
examples: A wave is a gesture.
He made a gesture.
The gesture meant stop.

more.def: A movement of your hands or body that shows a meaning or feeling.
examples: A wave is a friendly gesture.
He made a gesture for us to be quiet.
A thumbs-up gesture means good job.

easy.def: To have something come to you or to go and bring it.
examples: I get a new book today.
Please get your coat.
She got a letter.

more.def: To receive or obtain something, or to go and bring it back.
examples: My sister got a bike for her birthday.
Can you get the scissors from the kitchen drawer?
We get snow here almost every winter.
I get sleepy at night.
It gets cold in winter.
She got tall this year.

more.def: To change into a different condition or state.
examples: The sky gets dark when a storm is coming.
He got nervous before the spelling bee.
Ice cream gets soft if you leave it in the sun.

easy.def: A short trip for a rest.
examples: We went on a weekend getaway.
The cabin is a nice getaway.
A getaway to the beach.

more.def: A short trip, or a place you go to rest and be away from your normal life.
examples: We took a weekend getaway to the beach.
The cabin in the woods is a peaceful getaway.
A getaway to the mountains made a nice break from school.
